integrity: The proof works directly from the definition after every one-vertex deletion in both the crown graph and its complement. Two omitted vertices on the same bipartition side force disjoint omitted matching indices; robust domination then forces the n-3 thresholds, while an empty omitted side has the weaker n-2 threshold. The sole overlapping omission pattern is one common deleted pair. Sufficiency is checked by explicit neighborhood traces in the crown and in the complement, which consists of two cliques joined by a perfect matching.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is specific to crown graphs and does not classify arbitrary matching-deleted bipartite graphs.
The Cr_2=C_4 boundary is published in the introducing paper and is not claimed as new.
Finite verification is corroborative only; arbitrary n is proved symbolically.
A differently phrased or non-indexed crown specialization may exist.
title: Global stable location-domination of crown graphs
